div.head: Swer 4
div.ab: On ðone Drihten, ne teo ic N. ne for hete ne for hole ne for unrihtre feohgyrnesse, ne ic nan soðre nat, bute swa min secga me sæde, ⁊ ic sylf to soðe talige, ðæt he mines orfes þeof wære.

Ðæs að, þe his æhte bryideð: þæt he hit ne dæð ne for hete ne for hole. On ðone Drihten, ne te ic Ñ ne for hete ne for hole, ne for unrihtre feohgyrnesse, ne ic nan soðre nat, bute swa min secga me sæde, ⁊ ic sylf to soðe talige, þæt he mines orfes ðeof wære.

In omnipotenti Deo, non attraho mihi hoc N. pro amicitia uel inimicitia uel pro iniusto lucro, nec uerius inde scio, quam mihi sagemannus meus dixit, et ipse in ueritate loquor, quod pecunie mee latro fuit N.

(Eid dessen, der sein Werthstück im Anefang greift: dass er dies nicht aus Hass oder zur Verleumdung thut. B) Bei dem Herrn . . ., nicht bezichtige ich N. aus Hass oder zur Verleumdung oder aus ungerechter Geldgier, und ich weiss nichts Wahreres als wie mein Melder mir gesagt hat, und ich selbst als Wahrheit erachte, [nämlich] dass ér der Dieb meines Viehs gewesen sei.

(The oath of him who attaches his property: that he does not do it out of hatred or malice. B) By the Lord …, I do not accuse N. out of hatred or malice or out of unjust greed for money, nor do I know anything truer than what my informant told me and I myself hold to be true, [namely] that he was the thief of my cattle.

[I swear] by the Lord, [that] I do not accuse N. because of hatred or slander or out of avarice, and [I know] nothing more true than what my informant told me, and what I myself consider to be true: that N. stole my cattle.
div.note: U: translator unrecorded: check; B reads ‘te’ (so); H's ‘teo’ is corrected from ‘teo. c.’, and H's ‘hole’ altered from ‘hele’.

Cf. above 2¹; Gl Anefang 7; Diebstahl 23b; Klageeid 2. Although the rubricator and Q, independently of each other, assign this formula, like 2—3, 4, to the Anefang claim, the text contains nothing of this; and the following exculpation, c. 5, certainly does not concern Anefang

See Gl Hass 1. 2. Cf. Leis Wl 10. 14. In Germany: Zeumer Formulae (Mon. Germ., Leg. V) 628. The same pair hol ⁊ hete Wulfstan ed. Sweet Anglo-Saxon reader 109. Q did not understand hete and fell back on the more usual exhortation to justice; see that word in Gl 6ff.

Vgl. Wb 77: formelhafte Verbindung.—Ebd.: sagemannus, nicht sachlich zu verbinden mit ahd. sago, Fris. asega oder Westgot. sagio, sajo. Fränk. sagibaro ist ‘der Mann, der anzeigt’; E. Mayer Dt. Frz. Vfg. I 264. Das von Pol Mai damit konfundierte sacebor 13. Jhs. ist vielmehr ‘Träger (Inhaber, Vorbringer) der Anklage’; vgl. Steenstrup Danelag 329 und bær Godwine up his mal Ann. Agsax. 1052.—S. Gl Anzeige 8a

Cf. Wb 77: formulaic combination.—Ibid.: sagemannus, not to be connected in substance with OHG sago, Frisian asega or Visigothic sagio, sajo. Frankish sagibaro is ‘the man who informs’; E. Mayer Dt. Frz. Vfg. I 264. The 13th-cent. sacebor, which Pol Mai confuse with it, is rather ‘bearer (holder, bringer) of the accusation’; cf. Steenstrup Danelag 329 and bær Godwine up his mal Ann. Agsax. 1052.—See Gl Anzeige 8a
